chunks: Bode magnitude and phase of a first-order filter. The question: Draw mag/phase response of a first-order filter.
A Bode plot shows how a filter treats every frequency. It is two graphs stacked together.
The top one shows how much of the signal gets through (the magnitude), and the bottom one shows how much the signal is delayed (the phase).
Both use a logarithmic frequency axis, so each tick is ten times the last.
Imagine a road that runs flat for a while and then bends into a downhill slope of constant steepness. The flat part is the frequencies the filter lets through.
The bend is the corner frequency. The slope is how fast the filter shuts out higher frequencies.
In real life the bend is rounded, and the straight-line sketch is only an approximation.
With no load, the circuit is a divider between R and the capacitor's impedance 1 over (j omega C) . Low frequency: Z C to infinity so V out equals V in .
High frequency: Z C to 0 so V out to 0 .
Corner frequency: ( f c ): the frequency where the filter starts to cut. For an RC filter it is 1 over (2 pi RC) . Decibel (dB): a log scale for ratios.
0 decibels means unchanged, and -20 decibels means one tenth of the voltage. Decade: a factor of ten in frequency.
Phase: how far the output wave is shifted in time relative to the input, measured in degrees. Low-pass filter: passes low frequencies and cuts high ones.
Take an RC low-pass with a corner at 1 kilohertz. At 100 hertz the output is almost the full input (about 0 decibels) and the phase is about -6 degrees.
At 1 kilohertz the output is 0. 707 of the input (-3 decibels) and the phase is exactly -45 degrees.
At 10 kilohertz the output is about one tenth (-20 decibels) and the phase is about -84 degrees. That is the whole idea.
"For a first-order low-pass I'd draw magnitude in dB and phase versus log frequency.
Magnitude is flat at 0 decibels, is 3 decibels down at the corner f c equals 1 over (2 pi RC) , and then falls at minus 20 decibels per decade.
Phase goes from 0 to minus 90 degrees, with exactly minus 45 at the corner.
A high-pass is the mirror image: rising 20 decibels per decade up to the corner then flat, phase from +90 to 0, +45 at the corner."
